solutionSql:
INSERT INTO shipment_events (id, shipment_id, status, occurred_at)
SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.id) s.id, s.shipment_id, s.status, s.occurred_at
FROM staging_scans AS s
WHERE s.occurred_at > (SELECT last_loaded_at FROM load_watermark)
  AND s.status IS NOT NULL
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM shipments AS sh WHERE sh.id = s.shipment_id)
ORDER BY s.id, s.occurred_at;

UPDATE load_watermark
SET last_loaded_at = GREATEST(last_loaded_at, (SELECT MAX(occurred_at) FROM staging_scans));
sampleChecks: shipment_events goes from 678 to 705 rows, so 27 scans are loaded. Scan 1006, which sits exactly on the old watermark (2026-01-17 00:00 UTC), is not loaded. The duplicated scan 1007 appears once. Scans with NULL status (1016, 1027, 1038) and scans whose shipment is missing (9009, 9018, 9027, 9036) are not loaded. load_watermark moves from 2026-01-17 00:00 to 2026-01-19 18:00 UTC. After run 2, shipment_events and load_watermark are unchanged on sample, nulls and boundary.

rules.howSolved: WHERE occurred_at > (SELECT last_loaded_at FROM load_watermark), so an equal timestamp is excluded.
DISTINCT ON (s.id) with ORDER BY s.id, s.occurred_at keeps one row per scan id.
EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM shipments WHERE sh.id = s.shipment_id) keeps only scans whose shipment exists.
Read as MAX(occurred_at) over every staging_scans row, whatever its status or shipment.
GREATEST(current watermark, MAX(occurred_at)), so the watermark never moves backward; afterwards no staging scan is strictly newer, so run 2 adds nothing.

runsTwiceCheck: The whole load (INSERT, then the watermark UPDATE) ran twice in a row on sample, nulls and boundary. No error on either run. shipment_events and load_watermark after run 2 equal the state after run 1 on all three datasets.
ambiguities: 'set the watermark to the newest occurred_at' is read literally as a MAX, but the rule 'the watermark moves forward' implies no backward move. I used GREATEST. The two differ only when the staging maximum is older than the current watermark.
A scan with NULL occurred_at is not strictly newer, so it is never loaded. MAX skips NULL values, so it does not move the watermark.
The text says 'keep one copy' but not which copy wins if the two copies differ; DISTINCT ON keeps the one with the smaller occurred_at. On sample the copies are identical.
There is no guard for a NULL staging scan id, which would violate shipment_events.id NOT NULL. No error occurred on nulls or boundary, but the instruction does not address it.
notes: The starter is a bare UPDATE on load_watermark; my solution keeps an UPDATE with no WHERE, since load_watermark holds one row. The loaded rows are all after the old watermark and the 1000-series ids do not collide with the existing 1 to 678 events.
